skill.name: agents-md-audit
skill.description: Review agent instruction files for stale commands, broken paths, vague rules, possible secrets, and contradictions. Propose evidence-based corrections before editing.
skill.summary: Audit agent instructions with a local checker and evidence-based review before proposing a shorter version.
skill.author: agentkitco

content.user_title: Audit Agent Instructions for Accuracy and Risk
content.value_statement: Stale commands, broken paths, and vague rules make agent instruction files unreliable. This skill combines local checks with evidence-based review to propose shorter, accurate instructions.
actual_capabilities: Guide discovery of AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Claude rules, Cursor rules, and Copilot instruction files.
Flag files exceeding 150 lines, vague phrases, duplicate lines, and unfilled uppercase bracket placeholders.
Check backtick-formatted relative paths against the repository root, instruction file directory, and repository filenames.
Compare recognized inline npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, make, and just commands with package scripts, Makefile targets, and justfile recipes.
Flag possible secrets using regular expressions and report their categories without repeating matched values.
Guide manual contradiction review and propose a shorter version, while requiring approval before editing.
limitations: Checks are heuristic; an empty report does not prove instructions are correct or secure.
Command matching covers selected inline forms and simple root-level metadata; command existence does not prove successful or safe execution.
Contradictions, rule relevance, scoped placement, and actual command behavior require agent or human judgment.
The bundled checker requires Python 3.8 or later; without Python, the workflow relies on manual checks.

use_cases.title: Refresh Repository Instructions
use_cases.description: Review AGENTS.md after repository changes and identify outdated commands, missing paths, and instruction lines that need correction.

use_cases.title: Compare Assistant Rule Files
use_cases.description: Compare Claude, Cursor, and Copilot instructions for conflicting rules, duplication, and guidance that belongs in scoped files.

use_cases.title: Review Instructions Before Sharing
use_cases.description: Identify possible secrets, unresolved placeholders, and unverified commands before distributing repository instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Review One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit AGENTS.md for missing paths, vague rules, duplicates, and placeholders. Report evidence by line and wait for approval before editing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review a single instruction file.

prompt_templates.title: Check Documented Commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit CLAUDE.md against repository scripts and targets. Do not execute repository commands; mark runtime behavior as unverified and propose corrections supported by metadata.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: verify command references without running them.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Instruction Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Find agent instruction files and identify their readers. Compare rules for contradictions, redundant guidance, and scope problems, citing file names and line numbers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review instructions across several assistant tools.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Evidence-Based Rewrite
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit all instruction files using the checker and manual review. Separate required fixes, trimming suggestions, contradictions, and unverified commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: propose a shorter version preserving hard constraints, without adding rules or editing files before approval.

output_examples.input: An instruction file refers to a missing relative directory and repeats a long rule.
output: Must fix: The referenced directory does not exist relative to the repository root or instruction file.
Should trim: A repeated rule duplicates earlier guidance.
Proposed version: Retain one copy of the rule and remove the unsupported directory reference pending confirmation.

output_examples.input: An instruction file includes a possible credential and a deployment command.
output: Must fix: A possible secret was detected. Remove it and rotate the credential if it is real.
Not verified: The deployment command was not executed because deployment is excluded from the verification workflow.
Proposed version: Replace the credential with a reference to approved secret storage, subject to owner approval.

output_examples.input: Two instruction files require different package managers.
output: Contradictions: The instruction files specify different package managers.
Evidence needed: Confirm the intended package manager against repository configuration before selecting a replacement.
Proposed version: Keep one verified instruction in the appropriate scope after owner approval.

best_practices: Run the checker from the repository root or provide its root option so metadata and path checks use the intended repository.
Inspect command definitions before permitting execution, and keep deployment, migration, and deletion commands unverified.
Cite evidence for required fixes, redact possible secrets, and obtain approval before applying proposed edits.
anti_patterns: Treating an empty checker report as proof that instructions are complete, correct, or secure.
Executing repository commands solely because their names resemble harmless lint or test checks.
Replacing incident-driven constraints or editing instruction files before the owner approves the proposed changes.

faq.question: Which instruction formats does this skill review?
faq.answer: The workflow covers AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Claude rule files, Cursor rules, and GitHub Copilot instructions.

faq.question: Does the Python checker execute commands from instruction files?
faq.answer: No. It compares recognized command text with repository metadata. The broader workflow separately allows safe checks and excludes deployment, migration, and deletion.

faq.question: Does the skill edit files automatically?
faq.answer: The workflow requires a report and owner approval before editing. The checker only reads local files and prints findings.

faq.question: How are possible secrets handled?
faq.answer: The checker reports the detected category without printing the matched value. The workflow recommends removal and rotation when the credential is real.

faq.question: Can it find every contradiction or stale command?
faq.answer: No. Regular expressions and metadata checks have limited coverage. Contradictions and actual command behavior require additional review.

faq.question: What does the checker require?
faq.answer: It uses Python 3.8 or later and only the standard library. The workflow provides manual checks when Python is unavailable.
